event: Chicago Conservator founded by Ferdinand Lee Barnett — Chicago's first Black newspaper
The Broad Ax founded by Julius F. Taylor in Salt Lake City; Ida B. Wells becomes part-owner/editor of the Conservator
The Broad Ax moves to Chicago
Chicago Defender first issue (300 copies), founded by Robert S. Abbott
note: Day disputed (May 5 vs May 6); May 5 favored

event: Chicago Conservator ceases publication
Half-Century Magazine founded by Anthony Overton
Defender declares the 'Great Northern Drive,' its formal Great Migration campaign
Chicago Enterprise founded by Jacob R. Tipper
Associated Negro Press founded in Chicago by Claude A. Barnett
The Chicago Whip founded by William C. Linton (first issue)
Defender moves into 3435 S. Indiana Ave. headquarters
William C. Linton dies; Joseph D. Bibb succeeds as Whip editor
Bud Billiken Club co-created by Robert S. Abbott and Lucius Harper
Half-Century Magazine ceases (approx.); Chicago Bee founded by Anthony Overton (1925 or 1926)
Chicago Enterprise renamed Chicago World
Defender reaches ~250,000 weekly copies (peak)
The Broad Ax ceases publication
Olive M. Diggs becomes managing editor of the Chicago Bee (serves to 1946)
The Chicago Whip ceases publication
Chicago Crusader founded by Balm L. Leavell and Joseph H. Jefferson
Robert S. Abbott dies; nephew John H. Sengstacke inherits the Defender
Negro Digest first published; Johnson Publishing Company founded by John H. Johnson
JPC's first HQ inside the Supreme Life Building, 3501 S. Parkway
JPC buys building at 5619 S. State St.
Ebony first issue (25,000 copies, sells out); Era Bell Thompson joins JPC (1947)
Chicago Bee closes (1946 or 1947)
Alice Dunnigan becomes ANP Washington bureau chief (serves to 1961)
JPC relocates to 1820 S. Michigan Ave. (former funeral home)
Negro Digest ceases publication
Jet first issue (pocket-size weekly news digest)
Simeon Booker becomes first full-time Black reporter at The Washington Post
Lerone Bennett Jr. joins JPC (Jet associate editor)
Robert E. Johnson joins JPC (Jet associate publisher/executive editor)
Ben Burns fired from JPC (founding editor of Negro Digest, Ebony, Jet)
Moneta Sleet Jr. joins JPC as Ebony staff photographer
Jet publishes David Jackson's Emmett Till open-casket photographs; issue reprinted (first Jet reprint ever)
note: Issue date Sept 15 favored over Sept 22

event: Chicago Defender becomes a daily newspaper under John H. Sengstacke
MLK's 'Advice for Living' column begins in Ebony (runs 1957-58)
Lerone Bennett Jr. becomes Ebony executive editor; Ebony Fashion Fair traveling show begins
World News Service founded in Chicago by Hiram E. Jackson
Defender moves to 2400 S. Michigan Ave. (headquarters and plant to 2003)
Negro Digest revived under Hoyt W. Fuller
Associated Negro Press ceases operations (1964 or 1967)
Chicago Citizen founded by Gus Savage (as South End Citizen)
Sengstacke acquires the Pittsburgh Courier (final issue Oct 22, 1966); relaunched 1967 as the New Pittsburgh Courier
John H. Johnson receives NAACP Spingarn Medal
Moneta Sleet Jr. wins Pulitzer Prize for Feature Photography (Coretta Scott King at MLK's funeral)
Negro Digest renamed Black World
JPC moves into 820 S. Michigan Ave. (architect John Warren Moutoussamy)
Fashion Fair Cosmetics founded by Eunice Johnson
JPC buys WGRT ($1.8M), renames it WJPC - Chicago's first Black-owned radio station (operates to Dec 1994)
Black World terminated by Johnson
John H. Johnson named first African American on the Forbes 400
note: Widely repeated; not cross-checked against Forbes' list

event: N'DIGO founded by Hermene Hartman
South Street Journal founded by Ron Carter
John H. Johnson receives Presidential Medal of Freedom
Defender sale to Real Times approved Nov 4, 2002 (probate court); control transferred January 2003; Linda Johnson Rice becomes JPC CEO
Defender leaves 2400 S. Michigan; Fashion Fair peak sales ~$56M
John H. Johnson dies, age 87
Defender reverts from daily to weekly (Feb 13, 2008, Wednesday weekly; had cut five-day to four-day ~2006)
Ebony Fashion Fair show ends
820 S. Michigan sold to Columbia College Chicago
South Street Journal ceases
JPC announces Jet print ends (May 7, 2014); final print issue June 2014; moves to digital
Ebony and Jet sold to Clear View Group (photo archives retained by JPC)
820 S. Michigan designated Chicago Landmark; sold to 3L Real Estate ($10M)
JPC files Chapter 7 bankruptcy liquidation
JPC photo archive (~4M images) sold for $30M to Ford/Getty/MacArthur/Mellon/Smithsonian consortium
Chicago Defender publishes final print edition; digital-only thereafter
Fashion Fair Cosmetics sold for $1.85M to McKissack & Rogers
Bridgeman Sports and Media buys Ebony/Jet assets for $14M
Ebony and Jet relaunch under Bridgeman ownership
JPC archive ownership transferred to NMAAHC + J. Paul Getty Trust; public access target 2029
